output: Manchester City captain Vincent Kompany criticizes UEFA’s Financial Fair Play (FFP) regulations, arguing that they protect established elite clubs rather than preventing financial ruin. Kompany believes these rules hinder new challengers and maintain the dominance of traditional powerhouses like Manchester City. He cites City’s success under Sheikh Mansour’s ownership, attributing their achievements to significant investments that also benefit the local community and economy.

Jeff Williams, a 26-year-old England Sevens international who has scored 36 tries on the World Series circuit, has signed with Aviva Premiership side Bath for the upcoming season. Bath head coach Mike Ford and England Sevens head coach Simon Amor praised Williams' dynamic playstyle and his potential to contribute to Bath's attacking approach. Williams, whose background includes playing in South Africa and France, brings valuable experience to the team after helping England win the Tokyo Sevens tournament.

Director David Ayer revealed the first full look at Jared Leto portraying the Joker in "Suicide Squad," set for release in 2016, with Leto cutting his hair and shaving his face to fully embody the character. This will be the first time the Joker has been portrayed on screen since Heath Ledger's iconic performance, and the film will feature an ensemble cast including Will Smith, Margot Robbie, and other villains and anti-heroes. The movie is scheduled to hit theaters on August 5, 2016.

Three Florida corrections officers and a former officer trainee were charged with plotting to murder a former inmate as revenge for an earlier incident, according to court documents. They were recruited by an FBI informant who had infiltrated a Ku Klux Klan branch, and the suspects believed the FBI had carried out the killing when they were shown a staged crime scene. The men face up to 30 years in prison if convicted.

The conference call for Manny Pacquiao and Floyd Mayweather Jr. ahead of their fight was abruptly cancelled due to technical difficulties, affecting over 100 participants. During the brief call, Pacquiao managed to answer only one question about his training, to which he replied "very good." The call was rescheduled due to the frustration caused by the technical issues and the inability of some participants to join the conversation.

Serena Williams celebrated her 700th career victory at the Miami Open with a giant cake, following her victory over Sabine Lisicki in the tournament. Meanwhile, Andy Murray also received a celebratory cake to mark his 500th professional win. Williams advanced to the semi-finals and will face Simona Halep in the next round, while her sister Venus was defeated by Carla Suarez Navarro.

Beijing International Airport is constructing Terminal 1, set to become the world's largest terminal, to accommodate the significant rise in Chinese tourists traveling internationally. Designed by Zaha Hadid, this six-tier structure aims to enhance passenger experience through open spaces and seamless navigation, reflecting Chinese culture and landscape. With plans to handle 45 million passengers annually, Terminal 1 underscores China's growing influence in global tourism, following a dramatic increase in outbound travel from 10 million in 2000 to 109 million in 2014.

Manchester United's Wayne Rooney suffered a knee injury during their loss to Everton, which occurred in the closing stages of the match. Manager Louis van Gaal confirmed the injury but did not provide details on its severity. The defeat and Rooney's injury have intensified the competition for fourth place in the Premier League, with Manchester United now facing pressure from Liverpool.

Manchester City is reportedly interested in signing Jack Wilshere, who recently returned from an ankle injury and shared a humorous photo of his large grocery haul on Instagram. The photo showcased Wilshere's extensive shopping trip, including various cereals, eggs, baked beans, and corn on the cob, which he humorously captioned as his "day off" activities. Wilshere asked his followers for assistance in carrying the heavy groceries back to his home.

A Venezuelan woman named Marleni Olivo threw a mango inscribed with her contact information at President Nicolas Maduro during a rally, an act that gained viral attention. In response, Maduro offered Olivo an apartment as part of the country's housing program, fulfilling her long-standing wish to own a home. While some critics derided the incident, Maduro defended Olivo and used the event to highlight his housing initiatives.

Carlos Tevez, a former striker for Manchester United and City, believes scoring goals is more challenging in Serie A compared to the Premier League, despite his successful goal-scoring record in Italy. He criticizes the Premier League midfield as "non-existent" and praises the improved team structure at Juventus, suggesting they could achieve success similar to their 2008 Champions League victory. Tevez, who has scored over 80 Premier League goals and won multiple titles, contrasts the current Italian league with his previous experience in the Premier League, highlighting differences in defensive organization and team composition.

Jamie Carragher criticized Yaya Toure for ducking out of the way of Jason Puncheon's free-kick during Manchester City's loss to Crystal Palace, which effectively ended City's hopes of salvaging a positive result. Carragher argued that Toure should have done more to prevent the goal despite being part of a five-man wall. The criticism highlighted how other players in the wall were positioned to intercept the ball, while Toure appeared less engaged in the defensive effort.

A 50-year-old Australian man died after suffering a suspected heart attack at a hotel restaurant in Kuta, Bali. The man, from Seymour in Victoria, collapsed shortly after ordering breakfast and could not be revived; an autopsy was pending to confirm the cause. Kuta, known for its beaches and popularity among Australian tourists, was the location of the incident.

Former Australian cricket captain and commentator Richie Benaud, who passed away at 84 due to skin cancer, was honored with a private funeral service attended by close family and friends in Sydney. The event, requested to be kept small and private by Benaud himself, was followed by a memorial at the Australian Golf Club where his colleagues and former teammates paid tribute. Benaud, known for both his playing career and extensive work as a commentator, was widely respected and mourned by the cricket community worldwide.

A 16-year-old schoolgirl named Isobel Attwood has been missing from her home in Winchester, Hampshire for two days. She is believed to be in the company of a man in his 20s in Southampton, according to friends who posted on social media. Police are concerned for her welfare and are urging anyone with information to come forward.

If Manchester City do not qualify for the Champions League this season, key players like Sergio Aguero, David Silva, Joe Hart, and Yaya Toure stand to lose a collective £5 million in bonuses. The team currently sits in fourth place in the Premier League, with the top three securing automatic Champions League qualification, while the fourth place team must win a qualifying round. Manchester City's failure to secure these positions would jeopardize their chances of signing high-profile players like Paul Pogba, with Manchester United expected to compete for the same talent.

Martin Skrtel, a Liverpool defender, has denied rumors linking him to moves to Wolfsburg or Napoli, stating that his future remains at Liverpool despite his contract expiring in 2016. Skrtel's agent confirms that the only offer on the table is an extension to his contract, and there is no interest from German clubs as previously reported. Despite Liverpool's underwhelming season, Skrtel has committed to staying with the team by finalizing a new deal.

Cheryl Rios, a female CEO from Texas, sparked controversy when she claimed on Facebook that a woman cannot be president due to her "hormones" making it difficult for her to start a war. Her comments drew widespread criticism and were labeled as sexist and ignorant. In response, Rios defended her right to hold such beliefs while attempting to clarify that she supports women in other professions.

Mario Mandzukic, despite suffering injuries in a physical Champions League match against Real Madrid, is expected to be fit for the return leg at the Bernabeu. Atletico Madrid coach Diego Simeone confirmed that Mandzukic participated in training and is likely to be included in the lineup. Simeone also praised Antoine Griezmann's recent form and potential, indicating that the player is adapting well to his new position and showing significant improvement.

Chelsea head coach Jose Mourinho prepared his team to face Marouane Fellaini of Manchester United, only to learn from a hotel doorman that Fellaini wasn't playing due to being there to obtain tickets from Eden Hazard. The revelation came as a surprise to Mourinho, who then discovered that Fellaini's twin brother Mansour had been posing as him to take photos. Despite the confusion, Chelsea won the match 1-0 and moved closer to securing the Premier League title.

Dawn Milosky, a 45-year-old woman from Beachwood, New Jersey, was involved in a severe accident where her car overturned and caught fire shortly after she was rescued. Police responding to a tip about erratic driving found Milosky unconscious in her overturned 2006 Toyota Solara convertible, which was already smoking. After rescuing her, Milosky was revived using a defibrillator and CPR, and was later airlifted to Morristown Medical Center; she is reported to be in stable condition. Milosky has been charged with multiple offenses including driving while intoxicated and reckless driving.

A farmer in eastern China has become famous after his goat gave birth to a six-legged kid, nicknamed the "spider goat" by Chinese internet users. The baby goat, born 20 days ago, initially had six legs of similar length but as it grew, two of its front legs became shorter and cannot touch the ground. The farmer, Xiao Qibin, plans to let the unusual goat grow naturally without seeking veterinary intervention.

West Ham United are considering signing Javier Hernández, the Mexican striker who recently scored a crucial Champions League goal for Real Madrid against Atletico Madrid. Hernández, set to return to Manchester United after his loan ends, could be available for around £7 million. Alongside this, West Ham aims to strengthen its squad with young players, targeting midfielders Pedro Obiang and Fabian Schar, and forwards Moussa Konate.

Stuart McCall, the manager of Rangers, has dismissed any thoughts of his future with the club being decided before the end of the season, emphasizing that despite recent victories and improved morale, his team has yet to achieve anything significant in the Championship. McCall is confident in his contract extending until the end of the season and beyond, and is focused solely on winning matches, particularly in their upcoming game against Queen of the South. Additionally, Shane Ferguson, a Northern Ireland international on loan from Newcastle, is expected to join the team next week, though McCall is cautious about Ferguson's immediate contribution due to a recent knee injury.

Werder Bremen secured a 1-0 victory against Hamburg SV through a late penalty kick by Franco Di Santo, securing their position in the race for a Europa League spot. This win, coupled with Hamburg's loss, kept Werder in seventh place with 38 points, while Hamburg dropped to the last position with 25 points. New Hamburg coach Bruno Labbadia, making his debut under pressure to save the club from relegation, saw his side lose a player to a red card and slip further into the relegation zone.

A two-year-old boy fell into a cheetah exhibit at the Cleveland Metroparks Zoo after slipping between a 10 to 12-foot gap while being held by his parents, who then rescued him. The child suffered only minor injuries and was released from the hospital in stable condition. The zoo plans to press child endangerment charges against the parents due to eyewitness accounts suggesting the child was dangled over the railing.

A Russian TV channel, TV Rain, gave Hillary Clinton's 2016 presidential campaign video an 18+ rating due to concerns about the video featuring a gay couple holding hands, potentially violating Russia's anti-gay propaganda law. The channel feared breaking the law, which bans the promotion of non-traditional sexual relationships to minors, and thus marked the video to avoid legal repercussions. This decision came amid international criticism of the law and protests against it both domestically and internationally.

Siem de Jong, Newcastle United's 26-year-old midfielder who returned from a collapsed lung, played 45 minutes for the Under 21s in a 2-0 loss to Derby County. Despite initial optimism about his return to the first team, his subdued performance suggests he may not be ready for the upcoming match against Tottenham. Additionally, Facundo Ferreyra, another injured player on loan to Newcastle, also came on as a substitute at halftime.

Chef Ally Lees of Alfie Bird's restaurant in Birmingham created a massive omelette weighing 945g and containing 12,000 calories for an Easter promotion, requiring at least five people to finish it. The omelette, made from 150 eggs, boasts 16 times the recommended daily protein intake for a man but took an hour to cook due to its size. Chef Ally described it as the biggest omelette he has ever made and deemed it a successful challenge.

Three Olympic gold medalists from London 2012, including Jessica Ennis-Hill, Mo Farah, and Greg Rutherford, will participate in the Sainsbury’s Anniversary Games at the Olympic Stadium. The event features a three-day competition from July 24-26, including a world's only two-day Diamond League meeting, and aims to recreate the excitement of the 2012 Olympics. Tickets are now available for purchase online.

In a shocking discovery, police in Rio de Janeiro found a snack bar using the meat of stray dogs to make pastries, including the traditional Brazilian dish pastel. The owner, a Chinese man named Van Ruilonc, admitted to using the dogs, which he had captured himself, as filling for the pastries. This came to light during an investigation into potential human trafficking, revealing further abuses such as workers living in slave-like conditions and being forced to work long hours without pay.

Ebony Dickens, a resident of East Point, Georgia, threatened to shoot every white cop she saw on a Facebook post under a fake name, which led to a massive law enforcement effort involving local, state, and federal agencies. The post, which detailed plans to kill multiple officers and specifically targeted white police, resulted in Dickens' arrest and the seizure of a firearm and three computers during a search of her home. Dickens appeared in court and was charged with disseminating information related to terrorist acts.

PSV Eindhoven won the Dutch Eredivisie championship for the first time in seven seasons by defeating Heerenveen 4-1, putting them on 79 points and securing the title out of reach from second-place Ajax. Key to PSV's victory were goals from Luuk de Jong and a stunning free-kick from Memphis Depay, while the bottom team Dordrecht suffered another defeat, moving closer to relegation. Additionally, AZ Alkmaar secured a spot in the Europa League playoffs with a 3-1 win over ADO Den Haag.

An 11-year-old boy named Shiva was beaten to death by his head teacher, Lalit Verma, at Dwarika Prasad School in Railamau village, India, after allegedly stealing another student's pencil and eraser. The teacher admitted to slapping Shiva during questioning but the beating was so severe that the child died on arrival at the hospital from internal bleeding. This incident, which has sparked outrage, is not isolated; there have been multiple reports of extreme corporal punishment by teachers leading to the deaths of young boys in India.

A gastrointestinal illness affecting 100 passengers and five crew members has broken out on the Celebrity Infinity cruise ship, which is currently at sea. The Centers for Disease Control is investigating the cause, while the ship is en route to San Diego where CDC staff will board to assist. This is the third such outbreak on the Celebrity Infinity, with previous incidents occurring in 2006 and 2013.

A Boston Terrier named Gizmo, owned by Loren Mathieson, was seen performing an unusual walking technique after trying on new booties, which involved lifting his hind legs in a vertical stance. The video of Gizmo's gravity-defying walk went viral, garnering over 80,000 views and leaving many viewers amused. Gizmo reportedly performed this trick because he was uncertain about how to walk in his new footwear.

New Orleans has become completely smoke-free as of midnight on a recent Tuesday, following a city council ban that took effect on January 1. The ban, which passed unanimously, prohibits smoking in most public places such as bars, casinos, and restaurants. Despite some concerns from business owners about potential revenue loss and legal challenges from bar owners and Harrah's casino, the city aims to protect workers from secondhand smoke.

Manchester United secured a crucial victory over West Ham United in the Under 21 Premier League, moving four points clear at the top of the table. Despite taking an early lead through Josh Cullen's header, West Ham equalized within 12 minutes only for Manchester United to score twice, with Josh Harrop netting twice and Joe Rothwell adding another goal. The win came after a strong performance from captain Adnan Januzaj, who contributed to the team's comeback.

The Anglican Archbishop of Brisbane, Phillip Aspinall, has joined a local Catholic priest in advocating for the removal of Queensland's 'gay panic' homicide defense from the state's common law. This legal defense can reduce a murder charge to manslaughter if the defendant claims they felt threatened by sexual advances. In support of these calls, Aspinall also criticized instances of violence during anti-Islam rallies and church vandalism, urging people to resist reacting out of fear.

Sandra Bullock has been named the world's most beautiful woman by People magazine for 2015, marking her as the oldest recipient of the honor in its history. In the cover story, Bullock discusses her focus on being a good person and mother rather than solely on physical appearance, and shares a heartwarming moment with her son about aging gracefully. The selection reflects that beauty is not confined to a specific age group, as evidenced by Bullock's achievement and the inclusion of other diverse women in the "most beautiful" category.

An improvised bomb explosion near a U.N. vehicle in Garowe, Somalia, killed six people, including four UNICEF aid workers, on Monday morning, prompting strong condemnation from Somalia's president and the U.N. Al-Shabaab, an al Qaeda-affiliated group, claimed responsibility for the attack. The same day, three African Union troops died in an ambush in Somalia, and earlier in the week, Al-Shabaab had carried out a deadly attack on a Kenyan university, highlighting the ongoing violence and terrorism in the region.

Gary Saurage, the owner of Gator Country wildlife park in Beaumont, Texas, was called to capture a large 400-pound, 11-foot alligator from a family's backyard pond using only his hands. The alligator, which was particularly aggressive, was successfully removed and taken back to the park. The incident occurred after Art Williams spotted the gator in his garden during an Easter weekend walk and called for professional assistance to ensure everyone's safety.

In recent clashes between the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) militants and Turkish forces in Agri, eastern Turkey, five PKK militants were killed, one was injured, and four Turkish soldiers were wounded. Turkish Prime Minister Ahmet Davutoglu and President Recep Tayyip Erdogan condemned the attack, while Abdullah Ocalan, the jailed leader of PKK, had previously called for an end to violence and a focus on peace talks. This decades-long conflict has resulted in an estimated 40,000 deaths and remains a contentious issue in Turkey.

Two 18-month-old twin boys tragically died after accidentally falling into a canal in Yuma, Arizona. Search efforts lasting over an hour led to the discovery of the children, who were then airlifted to a local hospital but were pronounced dead upon arrival. Authorities believe the incident was accidental and no signs of foul play were found.

Orlando City, a Major League Soccer team coached by Adrian Heath, has shown interest in signing Javier Hernández, the Mexican international who recently struggled during his loan at Real Madrid. Despite eight European clubs also expressing interest, Hernández could potentially join Orlando City, which has a significant Latin-American fanbase, or face competition from teams like Southampton, Stoke, and West Ham. Meanwhile, Manchester United has revised their contract offer to young midfielder Andreas Pereira, whose father has received inquiries from clubs including Paris Saint-Germain, Juventus, and PSV Eindhoven, as the player remains undecided about his future with United.

Joel Burger, 24, proposed to his girlfriend Ashley King, 23, in a humorous twist, setting the stage for a Burger King-themed wedding. The couple, who have known each other since kindergarten, plan to serve drinks in personalized Burger King cups for their guests, though they acknowledge the restaurant may need to approve this idea. They met as young children when a motivational speaker humorously combined their names to form "Burger King," a nickname they have embraced throughout their relationship.

A secret police intelligence report from 1964 revealed that a hit band from the 1960s, along with disgraced BBC presenter Jimmy Savile, frequented a notorious pedophile brothel in Battersea, South West London. This information was discovered as part of an investigation into the flat, which was known to be used by pedophiles. Despite the connection between the band and Savile, a detective leading the inquiry stated that this alone was not enough to warrant further investigation without the benefit of hindsight.

Sadie, a German Shepherd from Alberta, Canada, has been caught on camera using her nose to turn on an electric organ and play piano sonatas, demonstrating remarkable musical talent. The video, showcasing her playful and determined approach to playing, has garnered over 12,000 views online. Sadie, who was adopted from an animal rescue shelter, enjoys learning new tricks, including playing the piano.

A smartphone thief named Ivan Balashov took a selfie in a Russian shop while browsing phones but was caught when police recognized him from the photo. After choosing a better phone, he tried to steal it but was stopped by shop security, who allowed him to leave with the phone before he fled. Police used his selfie taken in the shop to identify and arrest him shortly after.

A documentary trailer for "Amy: The Girl Behind the Name" has been released, featuring early footage of the late British singer Amy Winehouse discussing her musical journey. The film, which is set for UK release on July 3rd, aims to provide a sensitive and honest portrayal of Winehouse's life, including extensive unseen archive footage and previously unheard tracks. The documentary, directed by Asif Kapadia, has gained support from Winehouse's family and was produced by the same team behind the acclaimed "Senna" documentary.

The article suggests watching "The Big Bang Theory" for the return of talented actresses Christine Baranski and Laurie Metcalf as the show's mothers. It also highlights "Saturday Night Live" with Scarlett Johansson as the host, and "Mom" featuring an outstanding performance by Allison Janney. Additionally, the article mentions the season finales of "Backstrom," "Blue Bloods," and the start of a second season for "Younger."

Dame Maggie Smith's character, Violet, Countess of Grantham, may return in a new American show called "The Gilded Age," which is set in 19th-century New York and focuses on the wealthy elite. Additionally, Robert and Cora, Earl and Countess of Grantham, might also appear in the show as younger versions of themselves. The new series, created by Downton Abbey's Julian Fellowes, is expected to air on NBC possibly as early as September, pending finalization of plans.

Steven Gerrard is set to start for Liverpool in their FA Cup semi-final against Aston Villa at Wembley, marking what could be his final appearance at the national stadium before joining LA Galaxy. Manager Brendan Rodgers has selected Gerrard to lead the midfield, allowing him to potentially win a trophy and end his illustrious career with a victory. Despite being absent from the team due to a three-match suspension, Gerrard has shown readiness and special qualities that Rodgers believes will be crucial for the match.

A new Dr. Seuss book titled "What Pet Should I Get?" has generated significant interest, leading to an increased first printing from 500,000 to 1 million copies. This release marks the first original Dr. Seuss book since 1990 and features characters from his classic "One Fish Two Fish Red Fish Blue Fish." The manuscript was discovered in 1991 among the belongings of Theodore Geisel (Dr. Seuss) and only recently brought to publication.

Jessica Carey traveled over three hours to surprise her grandmother, Patty Lawing, with a tattoo of her younger self on Jessica's arm. The heartfelt gesture, captured on video by a relative, moved Patty to tears and elicited an emotional reaction. Jessica, along with her husband and two children, planned the surprise visit and tattoo to honor and celebrate Patty's youthfulness and beauty.

Annegret Raunigk, a 65-year-old German primary school teacher, is expecting quadruplets, making her the oldest known woman to carry such a pregnancy. Following 18 months of fertility treatment, she is set to give birth in weeks, having been artificially inseminated with donated sperm and eggs. Despite her advanced age, Raunigk remains optimistic about the birth and insists she feels fit and capable.

Japan's space agency, JAXA, plans to send an unmanned rover to the moon by 2018, aiming to join the select group of nations that have explored the lunar surface. The mission, which uses existing rocket technology and aims to develop soft-landing techniques, is estimated to cost between $83.4 million and $125 million and could be used for future manned missions to the moon or Mars. This move reflects Japan's desire to compete with regional rivals like China and India, which have achieved significant milestones in space exploration.

Three Brazilian football players, including Corinthians striker Paolo Guerrero, have contracted dengue fever, prompting Brazilian teams to take precautions such as using insect repellent during practice and checking facilities for mosquito breeding sites. The outbreak, which has caused over 460,000 cases in Brazil in 2015, has forced several players to miss crucial matches and has raised concerns among teams about the safety of their players. Health officials are working with clubs to control the situation and reduce the risk of further infections.

Manchester United striker James Wilson expressed his admiration for Wayne Rooney, Robin van Persie, and Radamel Falcao, stating that he would most like to adopt Rooney's skill in taking free-kicks, van Persie's movement, and Falcao's instinctive positioning. Wilson, who has made 16 appearances for Manchester United this season, trained alongside these experienced forwards and is using the opportunity to learn from them. He highlighted Rooney's daily practice of free-kicks, van Persie's ability to create space, and Falcao's predatory instincts as qualities he aims to incorporate into his game.

Archie Brown Jr., a 39-year-old van driver from Milwaukee, Wisconsin, was fatally shot at the scene after striking and killing a 2-year-old child who ran in front of his vehicle. Shortly after, a 15-year-old boy was also shot and later died, though his connection to the incident remains unclear. Police suggest the shooting may have been in revenge for the child's death, but no suspects have been arrested yet.

A child from Memphis, Tennessee, with a baby face, has gained over 3,000 Twitter followers by posting pictures of himself in "gang life" situations, including with guns and drugs, which has sparked criticism from the public. Despite the backlash, the child defended his actions, citing personal hardships and challenging his critics. Authorities are becoming more aware of how social media, including platforms like Twitter, can be used to promote gang culture.

Former Redgum frontman John Schumann criticized anti-Islam protesters for using his song "I Was Only 19" at Reclaim Australia rallies, which aimed to oppose sharia law and Islamization. Schumann stated that the song promotes compassion, tolerance, and inclusiveness, contradicting the rally's message. Violence erupted during the rallies, resulting in several arrests and minor injuries, prompting political leaders to condemn the violence and discourage spreading unfounded fears about religious practices.

Emmanuel Adebayor, a forward for Tottenham Hotspur, has denied rumors of a potential transfer and reaffirmed his commitment to the club via Twitter. Despite his past success and the signing of Harry Kane, Adebayor's recent performances have been criticized, and he has seen limited playing time this season. However, the 31-year-old striker remains dedicated to finishing his contract with Tottenham.

Stuart Pearce believes that Manchester City should give Manuel Pellegrini more time to improve the team's performance despite their recent struggles. Pearce, who has experience with the club as both a player and manager, attributes some of City's issues to the declining form of Yaya Toure and suggests that the squad needs significant refreshing. Despite the team's poor run, Pearce hopes that Pellegrini remains in his position, recognizing his experience in managing the team.

Steve Bruce remains optimistic about keeping Hull City in the Premier League despite a 2-0 loss to Southampton that leaves them struggling to avoid relegation. Bruce believes they need to secure between eight and nine wins from their remaining six matches, though several key players have been unavailable due to injuries. Bruce attributes the team's current form to these absences and remains confident they can still secure safety.

A full-scale terror alert was triggered in Reading when a member of the public reported seeing a barge with a fake missile launcher and a dummy in a balaclava on the Thames. Thames Valley Police and an Army bomb disposal team responded, only to find that the "weapon" was a non-threatening, purely ornamental model. The prankster's actions caused unnecessary panic, prompting local residents to criticize the stunt as both stupid and inappropriate given the current security climate.

Tiger Woods suffered an unusual injury during his play at the Masters when his club hit a tree root on the ninth hole, causing him to drop his club and cry out in pain. Although the four-time champion managed to continue playing and finished the tournament at 5-under-par, he admitted to popping a ligament in his right wrist, which he reinserted to allow him to complete the tournament. Despite his injury, Woods tied for 17th place, marking his best finish in over a year.

Iker Casillas asserts he will remain with Real Madrid despite potential competition from Manchester United's David de Gea, vowing to fight for the starting goalkeeper position. Casillas, who has dedicated his entire career to Real Madrid since joining as a 16-year-old in 1996, emphasizes his commitment to fulfilling his contract and supporting younger players if he is not chosen as the first-choice goalkeeper. He focuses on helping Real Madrid defend their Champions League title, acknowledging the strong competition in the upcoming semi-finals.

Embarrassing footage has surfaced of a failed missile launch in Russia, showing an S300 rocket barely lifting off before plummeting back to the ground, causing a small explosion and significant debris. This incident adds to the embarrassment for President Vladimir Putin, who has significantly increased the defense budget. The leaked video also highlights concerns over the reliability of Russian missile systems, following another rocket launch that killed six technicians near Donetsk in Ukraine several months prior.

Lancashire County Cricket Club has signed Australian all-rounder James Faulkner as their overseas player for the majority of the summer. Faulkner, who recently won the World Cup with Australia, will join the team after completing his Indian Premier League commitments and will replace Peter Siddle. The club's head coach, Ashley Giles, expresses excitement about Faulkner's arrival, praising his world-class status and strong record in first-class cricket.

Mary Kay Letourneau, once a teacher who had a relationship with her 13-year-old student leading to imprisonment, has since remarried and celebrated a 10-year marriage to her husband Vili Fualaau. In an upcoming interview with ABC's "20/20," the couple will discuss how they maintain their relationship despite the significant age gap and past controversies. Additionally, they will address Letourneau's plans to return to teaching and efforts to have her status as a registered sex offender changed.

Jamie Carragher traveled to Spain during the international break to watch his son James play in the Under 12s group of the Mediterranean International Cup. During his trip, Carragher participated in the opening ceremony and provided commentary for local television, sharing his experience on social media. Liverpool's young team faced local Catalan sides and the tournament, now in its 15th year, has featured many renowned players from various clubs.

Seattle-based filmmaker Gabriel Ng spent three months in Thailand to create a breathtaking six-minute video showcasing the country's beauty spots and everyday life. Filmed primarily on the island of Ko Samui using a remote control drone, the video features stunning coastal scenes, religious sites, and moments of daily life. The footage has gained significant attention on YouTube, with viewers praising the quality and comparing it to professional productions.

Peter Moores expressed his willingness to work with Michael Vaughan if he becomes England's new director of cricket, emphasizing that it is not a personal issue but rather about improving the team. Moores believes additional voices in the dressing room might not be necessary, depending on the new role's responsibilities. Despite the recent restructuring of England cricket management, Moores remains focused on his coaching duties and supports the emerging talent in the team.

Nottingham Forest intends to pursue a transfer for Blackburn's striker Jordan Rhodes, valued at £10 million, after a previous attempt in March was unsuccessful due to Blackburn's refusal. Manager Dougie Freedman believes a direct cash offer may persuade Blackburn to part with Rhodes, who has demonstrated his scoring ability by netting 70 goals over the past three seasons. Additionally, Blackburn's Gary Bowyer anticipates further interest in fellow striker Rudy Gestede, who recently scored 19 goals, including one against Forest.

In a video captured in Bahama, North Carolina, a trio of dogs—Sky (a Husky), Sadie (a brown and white Springer Spaniel), and Marshall (a black and white Springer Spaniel)—produce a unique musical ensemble by howling and barking in harmony. Starting with Sadie initiating the sounds, the Husky Sky follows with a more melodious howl, and both dogs engage in a musical interaction that includes barking, howling, and even playful interactions like mouth gestures. The video ends with the dogs howling in unison until their owner interrupts them, leaving the dogs looking surprised and disappointed.

The 'French Spiderman,' Alain Robert, climbed Dubai's 1,007-foot Cayan Tower without safety equipment, using only sticky tape and chalk for assistance, taking an hour and a half to reach the top. This daring feat, captured on video, demonstrates Robert's expertise in free-climbing skyscrapers, though it comes with a history of previous falls and legal troubles. Known for his stunts, Robert previously scaled the world's tallest building, the Burj Khalifa, though he adhered to safety protocols on that occasion.

An experimental cancer drug previously discontinued due to poor results showed promise in reversing Alzheimer's symptoms in mice, according to researchers at Yale University. The drug, AZD0530, works by blocking a process that damages nerve connections crucial for memory storage in the brain. Following these positive findings, human trials have been initiated to assess its effectiveness in Alzheimer's patients.

The article discusses the buildup of excitement around upcoming superhero films and shows, including the reveal of the appearance of the Vision from "Avengers: Age of Ultron," the release of the real Daredevil suit from the new Netflix series, and the announcement of a new character, Angel, for the upcoming "X-Men: Apocalypse." It also mentions the unveiling of Jamie Bell's character, The Thing, in the rebooted "Fantastic Four" movie, and the continued popularity of superhero content in media.

Veteran referee Kenny Bayless will officiate the highly anticipated boxing match between Floyd Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao, a role he has previously worked for both fighters in numerous bouts. However, former opponent Oscar De La Hoya criticizes Bayless's appointment, arguing that Bayless's history with Mayweather gives the American boxer an unfair advantage. Bayless has a reputation for breaking up close clinches in Mayweather's favor, which could potentially influence the outcome of the upcoming match.

Harry Kane's participation in the upcoming Under 21 European Championship is uncertain due to Tottenham Hotspur's scheduled post-season friendly in Malaysia. The club's manager, Mauricio Pochettino, is concerned about the potential for burnout, while the Football Association is in discussions with Tottenham about Kane's availability. Kane himself wishes to play for the Under 21 side but may be forced to miss the tournament to allow for adequate rest before the start of the new season.

A measles outbreak affecting over 130 people in California, primarily linked to visits to Disney theme parks, has concluded according to the California Department of Public Health. During the outbreak, 70% of those whose vaccination status could be confirmed were found to be unvaccinated, highlighting the importance of immunization. The outbreak, driven by the B3 strain, was controlled through extensive public health measures including prompt case investigations, vaccinations, and increased awareness among healthcare providers.

In Argentina, police are searching for a family of six who were photographed riding on a single motorbike without helmets, with two adults and four children aboard, in the city of San Miguel de Tucuman. This incident follows a similar case in Junín where a family of seven was captured on camera using the same method. Both families faced widespread condemnation from social media users and public outcry over the dangerous and irresponsible behavior.

A 44-year-old woman named Andrea McVeigh was seriously injured when she was struck by a cyclist while walking on the pavement in Bermondsey, London. The cyclist fled the scene after hitting Ms. McVeigh, leaving her with severe facial injuries including two three-inch gashes to her forehead. Police have released CCTV footage of the cyclist and are appealing for information to catch him.

The headstone of Hillary Clinton’s father, Hugh Rodham, was found tipped over in a cemetery in Scranton, Pennsylvania, just days after Clinton announced her candidacy for the presidency. The incident has sparked speculation about potential political motives, with some believing it could be related to Clinton’s campaign, though police suspect it may be vandalism rather than weather-related damage. Local funeral director Neil Regan and resident Paul McGloin, who regularly tends to the gravesite, both believe the most likely cause is vandalism.

A California woman, Beatriz Paez, was recording police activity when a U.S. marshal took her phone, smashed it with his foot, and kicked it away, according to a video of the incident. Paez, who was standing several homes away from the main action, claims she was told to stop recording but asserted her right to do so, which led to the marshal's aggressive response. Following the incident, Paez has filed a complaint and is considering legal action against the marshal's actions, which she considers illegal as she was not obstructing an investigation or arrest.

Max, a 18.5-inch-tall corgi-Siberian husky cross, has been abandoned and is now at the Dogs Trust in Basildon, Essex, where he has become a favorite among the staff. Max's small stature belies his gentle and intelligent nature, making him an ideal pet despite his mixed-breed status. The Dogs Trust notes that the popularity of wolf-like dog breeds, influenced by TV shows like Game of Thrones, often leads to abandonment when owners are unprepared for the specific care needs of these dogs.

Chilean pickpockets have emerged as the most effective thieves operating in central London, targeting wealthy tourists in areas such as the West End. According to undercover police, these gangs, often consisting of three to six individuals, use sophisticated methods to blend in and steal high-value items from their victims. The police have noted that these organized groups move between major European cities to avoid detection and have reported a significant reduction in thefts in monitored areas.

In a severe car accident in Southam, Warwickshire, a young driver survived a crash where his vehicle flipped onto its roof and he became trapped underneath. Despite suffering multiple injuries, including head, chest, and leg fractures, the man remained conscious throughout the rescue operation, which took 25 minutes by firefighters using specialized equipment. The incident resulted in significant vehicle damage and required the assistance of multiple emergency services, ultimately leading to the man's transport to University Hospital Coventry and Warwickshire.

Fly-tippers have dumped an astonishing 40 tonnes of industrial waste along the roadside in the Suffolk village of Walsham-le-Willows, prompting a significant cleanup effort expected to cost thousands of pounds. Described by a police officer as the worst case of fly-tipping he has seen in his 28-year career, the incident involved the use of three tractors and trailers to deposit the waste, including materials from the carpet and veterinary industries. Local authorities and environmental agencies are working together to address the issue and prevent future incidents of fly-tipping.

At Toronto's Pearson International Airport, a man who refused to comply with security staff was tasered and subdued after attempting to enter a restricted area; the incident was captured on video by a bystander, showing the man mumbling and holding a black briefcase as he was Tasered, after which he was handcuffed and transferred to a nearby hospital under Canada's Mental Health Act. Authorities did not seek criminal charges against him.

Serbia's President Tomislav Nikolic's government jet had to return to Belgrade after the co-pilot accidentally spilled coffee on the instrument panel, causing the plane to lose altitude and resulting in a turbulent descent. The co-pilot, Bojan Zoric, admitted that he mistakenly activated an emergency function while cleaning up the spill, which led to the loss of autopilot control. Zoric's license was suspended following the incident, and an investigation found that one of the engines also stopped working during the return journey.

In South Africa, over 300 suspects have been arrested in connection with violent attacks targeting foreigners, which have forced thousands to seek refuge in temporary shelters. The government condemned the attacks and credited law enforcement for preventing further casualties, though xenophobia remains a significant issue in the country. Despite the violence, there has been an outpouring of support from ordinary South Africans and organizations like the Gift of the Givers charity, which offers assistance to those affected and maintains a shelter ready to accommodate refugees if needed.

A skier named Zach Birnie captured harrowing footage of himself becoming entangled in an avalanche while skiing off-piste in Revelstoke, Canada. Despite the terrifying experience, Birnie managed to escape with only a slight shoulder injury, thanks to shouting for help and instinctively trying to find the surface of the snow. Experts attribute the avalanche to the combination of fresh snow and steep terrain, advising those caught in a similar situation to try to escape the avalanche area and adopt specific survival techniques.

On the hottest day of the year, two bare-chested men in their 20s attempted to rob an Esso petrol station in Caterham, Surrey, forcing their way into the manager's office to search for cash but were interrupted by staff and fled without taking any money. Police released CCTV images of the suspects, urging the public to help identify them. A third man was later arrested but released on bail.

The Lada Niva 4x4, starting at £13,395 on the road, is gaining popularity as an alternative to the discontinued Land Rover Defender, thanks to its robust design and affordability. Despite being a Russian brand once subject to ridicule, the Niva has won fans worldwide for its reliable performance and rugged appearance, even available in a compact van format for £10,590. However, while the car offers no frills and a simple plastic interior, it has also been noted for its political connections, as evidenced by Russian President Vladimir Putin driving one with a German engine installed in 2009.

A lawsuit has been filed against the nation's largest supplier of HIV and AIDS medical care, the AIDS Healthcare Foundation, accusing the company of a $20 million scam over 12 states involving kickbacks for patient referrals to boost funding from Medicare and Medicaid. Former managers claim the company paid employees and patients $100 bonuses for referring positive test results and implemented this scheme starting in 2010. Despite these allegations, the foundation's president maintains they have not done anything wrong and argues that the government’s refusal to intervene supports their stance.

Liz, a bearded dragon owned by Shannen Hussein, has been filmed nodding her head in response to being asked if she's hungry, showcasing her apparent understanding of English. Following the positive reinforcement, Liz was rewarded with a superworm treat, which she reportedly adores. Shannen, who runs a popular social media channel featuring her various pets, including a lamb named Winter who has also gained internet fame, shares daily life with her diverse menagerie on her online platforms.

A West Virginia man named Travis Hatfield gained viral attention for posting a video of him singing a George Jones song to his uncle, Jamie Joe Cline, who has Down syndrome. The heartfelt performance, which has been viewed over 410,000 times, showcases their weekly musical duets and has inspired Travis to pursue a career in country music. Travis now has national recognition and aspirations to perform on The Voice and release an album.

Nik Wallenda, the daredevil from the "Flying Wallenda" family, will attempt an unprecedented high-wire walk on April 29 over the moving 400-foot Orlando Eye observation wheel in Florida. This stunt, which involves walking atop the turning wheel, sets itself apart from previous challenges due to the larger scale and the absence of a safety tether. Wallenda, known for his daring feats such as crossing the Grand Canyon and performing blindfolded between Chicago skyscrapers, plans to walk a portion of the wheel's circumference during its operation.

Medhi Benatia, a central defender for Bayern Munich, is likely to miss both legs of the Champions League quarter-final against Porto due to a muscle injury sustained during a German Cup match. This injury, which could keep him out for two to four weeks, adds to Bayern's already lengthy injury list. Despite the setback, Bayern Munich remains a strong contender for multiple titles, including the Bundesliga championship, with some players returning to training.

Bayern Munich secured a dominant 6-1 victory over Porto in the Champions League quarter-final second leg, advancing to the semi-finals and continuing their exceptional form under Pep Guardiola. This performance brought their season total to 115 goals, with the team showing no signs of slowing down, as they still have five Bundesliga matches, a German Cup semi-final, and potential Champions League games to go. At their current pace, Bayern could end the season with an astonishing 141 goals, putting immense pressure on other European teams to match their scoring prowess.

Fernando Torres credits Diego Simeone as the key figure behind Atletico Madrid's recent success and their upcoming Champions League match against Real Madrid. Since Simeone's leadership, Atletico Madrid has become one of Europe's top teams, having not lost to Real Madrid in six consecutive matches. Torres emphasizes that Simeone's understanding of the team's strengths and weaknesses is crucial to their performance.

A light aircraft crash occurred near Loch Etive in Argyll, Scotland, resulting in the discovery of two bodies among the wreckage. The plane lost contact with ground control while en route from central Scotland to Tiree Island and was last seen diving. Search efforts involved lifeboats, helicopters, and police, with ongoing inquiries to determine the exact circumstances of the crash.

A bus shattered the windscreen of a Boeing 777 passenger jet at Tashkent airport in Uzbekistan, causing significant damage and potentially delaying numerous passengers. This incident, along with recent collisions involving Ryanair and British Airways, highlights the increasing frequency of such accidents at major airports around the world. These incidents often result in significant disruptions to travel schedules without causing injuries, though they raise concerns about safety protocols and human error in airport operations.

An off-duty Secret Service agent, Arthur Baldwin, was arrested in Washington D.C. for attempting to break into a house and causing property damage at midnight, leading to the revocation of his security clearance and his placement on leave. His arrest follows another recent incident involving a high-ranking supervisor who was placed on leave due to alleged misconduct, both events bringing embarrassment to the agency responsible for presidential protection. Additionally, the inspector general is investigating another incident where two senior officials were accused of entering a restricted area of the White House while intoxicated.

Israel is developing a unique tunnelling detection system, designed to accurately identify tunnel activities from a distance without false alarms, following extensive proposals evaluation by the Israeli Ministry of Defense. The system, costing approximately £2.3 million per mile to install, aims to enhance security along the Gaza-Israel border, where numerous tunnels have posed threats. Initial tests have been successful, with further results expected soon.

A primary school headteacher has implemented a water-only drink policy during school hours to promote long-term pupil health, but the move has sparked a campaign by parents who argue it is too restrictive and limits children's choices. Parents, such as Samantha Moore and Anela, have launched a petition to overturn the ban, arguing that children should be allowed to drink other beverages like fruit juice. The school defends the policy as beneficial for students' health, though it faces opposition from those who believe it should be up to parents to decide their children's drink choices.

Paul Smith has secured a significant fight against undefeated Andre Ward on June 20 in Oakland, California. This opportunity comes after Smith's previous attempts to challenge for the WBO title were unsuccessful, while Ward has not fought since November 2013. Despite the potential ring rust, Smith is eager to prove himself against one of boxing's top pound-for-pound fighters.

German Chancellor Angela Merkel spent Easter on the island of Ischia in Italy, where she and her husband, chemist Joachim Sauer, typically stay at the luxurious five-star Miramare Spa Hotel. Despite the cool weather and lack of sunshine, Mrs. Merkel focused on healthy activities like Pilates and vegetarian meals rather than swimming or sunbathing. Merkel's husband, known for avoiding the spotlight, was present but kept a low profile as he often does during their annual holiday.

Ander Herrera, a Manchester United midfielder, has scored several goals without looking at the ball or the goal, including a brace against Aston Villa where his eyes appeared shut during both goals. This unusual shooting technique has been observed in multiple matches, though Herrera did hit the ball with his eyes open in a game against Yeovil in January. Despite his unorthodox method, Herrera has shown significant potential, impressing his coach with his kicking technique, though he is advised to improve his composure and ball control.

A 23-month-old toddler tragically died after being struck by her father's pickup truck in the driveway of their North Las Vegas home. The father and other family members were unaware that the toddler had ventured outside. The incident was ruled an accident, and no charges were filed.

The University of Connecticut baseball team has welcomed 5-year-old Grayson Hand, a child battling leukemia, as its newest member with the help of Team IMPACT. Grayson will join the team, have his own locker, and attend games and practices, while his sister Sophie has been named an honorary cheerleader. This partnership, according to Grayson's father, symbolizes the family's experience of collective support during their journey with cancer.

A passenger on a London Midland train discovered excrement in a newspaper on the floor, causing significant delays and the cancellation of a train service between Lichfield Trent Valley and Longbridge. London Midland has pledged to provide CCTV footage of the alleged perpetrator to the police for investigation. The incident prompted the train to terminate early at Birmingham New Street for cleaning, apologizing to affected passengers for the disruption.

James Rodriguez, who moved to Real Madrid for £60 million from Monaco last summer, has proven to be a valuable asset to the team, helping them win 80% of their matches when he is in the lineup, according to Spanish newspaper Marca. Meanwhile, despite a controversial yellow card for Cristiano Ronaldo, Real Madrid continues to impress. In Italy, Roberto Mancini is reportedly planning a significant summer overhaul of Inter Milan's squad, aiming to sign eight new players from a shortlist of 21 candidates, which includes several Premier League stars and some top European talent.

A Florida man named Kenneth Crowder, believed to be under the influence of the powerful drug Flakka, attacked a police officer after being tased twice, claiming he was God and attempting to stab the officer with a police badge. Crowder was arrested and charged with battery on a law-enforcement officer, resisting with violence, and assault with a deadly weapon on a law-enforcement officer. Flakka, a potent synthetic drug similar to cathinone, has been linked to numerous incidents of erratic and violent behavior in Florida.

During a Russian Premier League match between Arsenal Tula and Torpedo Moscow, a brawl among fans led to the game being suspended for seven minutes. Torpedo fans broke barriers, threw seats, and fought with law enforcement and stewards, causing the referee to halt the match. Following the incident, Torpedo faces severe punishment from the league due to repeated hooliganism and racist behavior by their supporters.

High school girls in Huizhou, China, are undergoing military-style dagger drills as part of their self-defense training under the guidance of former special forces soldier Inspector Tan. Although the knives used in the training are fake and pose no danger, the girls are learning techniques that could be life-saving, using any sharp object available to them, including everyday items like chopsticks and forks. The training, which involves a series of eight movements and takes five days, is widely popular among the participants and aims to equip students with skills to handle dangerous situations.

AP McCoy, the champion jockey with a record of winning the title every year since 1997, is urging the nation to support his final chance at winning the Grand National with his mount Shutthefrontdoor, which would be a fairytale ending to his career. Despite the high odds, McCoy remains optimistic, acknowledging the unpredictability of the sport but emphasizing his unwavering belief in the dream. Should Shutthefrontdoor win, McCoy has vowed to retire immediately, ending his 25-year career.

John Isner advanced to the Miami Open semifinals with a straight-sets victory over Kei Nishikori, becoming the first American man to reach this stage since 2011. In the other semifinal, Andy Murray will face Tomas Berdych, with added tension as both players have former coaching connections that led to conflict in a previous match.

Former German football legend Franz Beckenbauer criticized Bayern Munich's performance in their Champions League quarter-final loss to Porto, comparing it to players taking "sleeping pills." He specifically targeted Brazilian defender Dante, jokingly suggesting he wore "ski boots." Despite the harsh words, Beckenbauer remained optimistic about Bayern's chances, attributing their poor performance to just a couple of bad days rather than a systemic issue.

A 21-year-old man named Arnold Quintero from San Antonio, Texas, has been arrested for allegedly imprisoning, beating, sexually assaulting, and burning a 13-year-old girl with a lighter over several weeks. The girl identified Quintero from a photographic lineup after being held in a "trap house" and subjected to physical and sexual abuse. He faces multiple charges including aggravated sexual assault of a child and possession with intent to deliver, with some charges having already been bonded out while others remain pending.

In Week 12 of the Betway Premier League, Michael van Gerwen and Gary Anderson each won and lost one game, experiencing a mix of success and setbacks. Van Gerwen secured a dominant 7-0 victory over James Wade and advanced to the May play-offs at the 02, but later lost to Gary Anderson. Anderson, after an initial loss to Stephen Bunting, won a thrilling match against Van Gerwen with an impressive average of 105.94.

Training consultant Jay Rutland, husband of billionaire Tamara Ecclestone, earned just £65 a week from his company Brigante Business Developments, which reported total net assets of £3,378 for the year ending July 2014. Despite his low earnings, Rutland and Ecclestone, whose family is worth an estimated £3 billion, live a lavish lifestyle, including a £7 million wedding and £70,000 farmyard-themed birthday party for their daughter.

A Chinese man named Jia Binhui, diagnosed with leukemia and unable to afford traditional medical treatment, has resorted to a homemade alternative therapy involving lying over hot coals in his backyard, hoping the high temperatures will kill off his cancer cells. Despite coming from a poor farming background, Jia managed to undergo a bone marrow transplant through donations but has since run out of funds for further treatment. Jia, who recently married his long-term girlfriend, continues this unconventional method while expressing determination to improve his condition before seeking professional medical advice again.

Leroy Fer, a Dutch midfielder for Queens Park Rangers, is expected to return to the squad ahead of their match against West Ham due to recover from a knee injury. Manager Chris Ramsey hopes to include Fer, though he acknowledges the player is not yet at full fitness. QPR is aiming to use this opportunity to bolster their chances against relegation, with several other players also returning to fitness.

In the final kilometre of the Scheldeprijs race, Team Sky teammates Sir Bradley Wiggins and Geraint Thomas escaped a major crash involving around 50 riders, while their teammate Elia Viviani was injured and taken to the hospital for x-rays after hitting the barriers. The crash affected Team Sky's sprint strategy, with Katusha's Alexander Kristoff winning the race as only 14 riders contested the sprint finish.

Before their FA Cup semi-final against Liverpool, Aston Villa's players received supportive messages in their dressing room at Wembley Stadium. Young player Jack Grealish tweeted one such message, which read, "You have to put up with the rain to see the rainbow! Three seasons of rain boys, time to find the end of that rainbow and prove we're the pride of the Midlands!" Other players, including goalkeeper Brad Guzan, also shared encouraging messages, with Guzan's instructing the team to "fight like Lions."

A 12-year-old boy named Hanghang in central China suffered severe injuries when his old mobile phone exploded while charging, exposing parts of his jawbone and embedding fragments in his arms and legs. Experts attribute such explosions to improper charging or damaged batteries, emphasizing the importance of disconnecting the phone from the charger during use and ensuring the battery is not overcharged. Hanghang, who called an ambulance on his own after the incident, is undergoing multiple surgeries to repair the extensive damage.

Mike Rowe, host of "Somebody's Gotta Do It," highlights the work of Chad Pregracke, founder of Living Lands & Waters, a nonprofit dedicated to cleaning U.S. waterways. Since its inception in 1998, the organization has collected over 8.4 million pounds of trash through the efforts of more than 87,000 volunteers. Pregracke aims to remove an additional 500,000 pounds of trash in 2015 and encourages others to join in by visiting LivingLandsAndWaters.org/Get-Involved/.

The ancient Tuscan town of Balestrino, dating back to the 11th century, was captured in a drone video showcasing its eerie beauty and mysterious history. Once home to 800 inhabitants and owned by the Benedictine abbey of San Pietro dei Monti in the 1100s, the town was largely abandoned due to seismic instability, with an 1887 earthquake measuring 6.7 on the Richter scale causing significant damage. Today, considered the most famous abandoned location in Italy, the town is shrouded in mystery and local folklore, with some structures still standing while others have fallen into disrepair.

At an emotional event in Anaheim, California, director J.J. Abrams and the cast of "Star Wars: Episode VII – The Force Awakens" unveiled the trailer for the new film, receiving a warm welcome from the audience who broke into applause. The event featured introductions of new characters, such as the BB8 droid, and hints at the film's setting on the planet Jakku. Director Abrams also noted that the movie would feature more practical effects rather than relying heavily on CGI, aiming for a more tangible experience for viewers.

Toronto's former Mayor Rob Ford announced he would undergo surgery to remove a cancerous tumor in his abdomen, having previously undergone chemotherapy and radiation treatment. Ford, who had been re-elected to his former council seat after quitting his mayoral bid due to health issues, expressed gratitude for the support he received and hopes to return to work in September. Despite his health challenges, Ford maintained a positive outlook, emphasizing his gratitude and the importance of second chances in life.

At the University of Cape Town, a long-standing campaign to remove the statue of Cecil Rhodes culminated in its removal, as the university received permission from the heritage authority. This action was seen by many students as a step towards a more Afrocentric educational environment, reflecting a desire to move away from symbols of colonialism and racism. However, the decision sparked controversy among Afrikaner groups who viewed the statue as a representation of historical figures essential to South African history, arguing that removing such monuments erases important parts of the nation's past.

Michael Phelps returned to competitive swimming after a six-month suspension and won the 100 meters butterfly event at the Arena Pro Swim Series in Arizona. The 18-time Olympic gold medalist, who was banned following a drink-driving conviction, expressed joy at being back in competition. Despite missing the upcoming World Championships, Phelps announced his intention to compete in the 2016 Olympics in Rio de Janeiro.

A woman was found hanging from a fire escape in Crown Heights, Brooklyn, for over an hour on Sunday morning. Neighbors were traumatized by the discovery, with some initially believing it to be a Halloween prank. The victim, whose identity remains undisclosed, had a history of mental health issues and was known to be struggling before her death.

Lyon reclaimed the top spot in Ligue 1 after securing a 2-2 draw against Saint-Etienne in a thrilling Rhone Valley derby, thanks to goals from Clinton N'Jie and Christophe Jallet. Meanwhile, Lille maintained their pursuit of a top-four finish by defeating Bordeaux 2-0, with goals from Nolan Roux and Adama Traore. Additionally, Montpellier secured a narrow 1-0 victory over Caen through an early header by Brazilian defender Hilton, helping them move up to seventh place while leaving Caen in 13th.

Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger admits he did not anticipate that Hector Bellerin and Francis Coquelin would become such crucial players in the team's recent push for the Premier League title. Bellerin, who was previously at Watford on loan, scored a crucial goal against Liverpool, while Coquelin has emerged as a key defensive midfielder. Despite initial doubts about their abilities, Wenger praises both players for their performances and the mental quality they display under pressure.

Fox is developing a two-hour remake of the 1975 cult classic "The Rocky Horror Picture Show" for television, with plans to celebrate the film's 40th anniversary. Directed and executive-produced by Kenneth Ortega, the special will feature a cast yet to be announced and is set to be filmed in advance rather than aired live. The project, produced by Fox 21 Television Studios and The Jackal Group, follows previous attempts to adapt the film into a television special and will premiere sometime in the future.

Roma FC has been ordered to close part of their stadium for their next home game due to offensive banners displayed by fans during a match against Napoli. These banners insulted the mother of a Napoli fan who died in violent clashes following a previous match. In response, the club president condemned the fans' behavior and called for respect and unity.

Ellen White scored a spectacular goal for Notts County against her former club, Arsenal, by taking a free kick from the edge of the box and firing it into the corner. This moment was particularly satisfying for White, not only because it was a perfect execution of a set piece from training but also because it was scored against her previous team. Despite this impressive performance, White later missed a penalty, and the game ended in a draw when Arsenal scored an equalizing goal near the end.

Arsene Wenger maintains he has no regrets about not signing Eden Hazard in 2012, despite the Chelsea forward becoming one of the Premier League's standout players and winning the transfer of the year for joining Chelsea for £32 million. Wenger attributes the missed opportunity to financial constraints and the high costs involved at the time. Despite the regrettable decision, Wenger now praises Hazard's improved performance and maturity, acknowledging that he is in contention for the Player of the Year award, with Arsenal's Alexis Sanchez also considered a strong contender.

Stephen Akers-Belcher, the Mayor of Hartlepool, was dismissed from his care manager role at Newcastle City Council after claiming to take time off for a funeral but being found at HMS Warrior, 323 miles away. The council denied he was dismissed for whistleblowing, stating that an investigation into his claims found no further action was needed. Akers-Belcher maintained he did not attend the warship for a funeral and claimed to have been dismissed for whistleblowing despite the council's denial.

Dr. John Parker, a humanitarian doctor who had been working in an Ebola treatment clinic in Sierra Leone, tested negative for the Ebola virus after showing symptoms of an influenza-like illness upon returning to Sydney. He was taken to Westmead Hospital, where tests confirmed he did not have Ebola, and no further testing was deemed necessary. Dr. Parker had followed protocol by notifying authorities as a precaution after experiencing symptoms while staying at an airport hotel.

A schoolboy named Frankie Franz, inspired by Barcelona's Martin Montoya, successfully replicated a 27-yard goal into a basketball hoop from a video he watched, impressing both his mother and himself. The nine-year-old, who plays for Dagenham and Redbridge Football Club, managed to score the trick shot twice, demonstrating remarkable skill and confidence. Frankie dreams of playing for top clubs like Real Madrid or Barcelona, having shown exceptional talent from a young age.

The Wisden–MCC Cricket Photograph of the Year 2014 short-list features captivating images of cricket players ranging from amateur enthusiasts to professional stars, capturing moments from around the world. Notably, Matthew Lewis won the competition with an image of West Indies player Dwayne Bravo making an extraordinary catch during the ICC World Twenty20. The collection also includes heartwarming and dramatic scenes such as children playing cricket on a Bangladesh rubbish tip and the intense moment of Australian batsman Philip Hughes being struck by a ball.

In a custody dispute, a New Jersey judge ruled that a mother's decision to take her 11-year-old daughter to a Pink concert was not evidence of bad parenting, despite the father's objections. The judge found the performances to be appropriate for a preteen and noted that the mother had made an informed decision after reviewing the content. The judge emphasized that the mother did not exceed reasonable parental judgment and that the concert did not pose any risks to the child.

Salcombe, a coastal town in Devon, has overtaken London in average property prices, with the average cost of a property in Salcombe reaching £671,759, compared to £638,217 in London. The waterfront properties in Salcombe are particularly expensive, with an average value topping £2 million, surpassing some of London’s priciest areas such as Notting Hill and Regent’s Park. As a result, Salcombe has become a sought-after destination for both buyers and tourists seeking a luxurious seaside experience.

Celtic have expressed dissatisfaction with the ticket prices set by the Scottish FA for their upcoming Scottish Cup semi-final against Inverness Caledonian Thistle at Hampden Park. The club particularly criticized the £23 price for North Stand tickets, arguing it was too high for many supporters. In response, the Scottish FA stated that all four participating clubs were consulted on the pricing, which had remained unchanged for four years, and that revenues were distributed evenly among the teams.

Rebecca Rice, a 16-year-old student struggling with exam nerves, was allowed to bring her pet Labrador, Holly, into her GCSE French oral exam at Bodmin College in Cornwall. This unconventional support helped Rebecca remain calm during the five-minute test, as recommended by her teacher, Lorette Esteve, who noted that previous calming strategies like bringing drinks or lucky items hadn't worked for Rebecca.

Anders Lindegaard, the goalkeeper for Manchester United, recently shared a photo of himself and his wife Misse Beqiri enjoying the English sun, reminding fans of their happy marriage. Lindegaard, who has had limited playing time with the team, has been linked to potential transfers due to his struggle for minutes. Off the pitch, however, he and his wife, a popular Swedish model, are thriving and have a son together.

Spanish goalkeepers David de Gea and Victor Valdes took a much-needed break from the pressures of the season by visiting a theme park in England. Their recent performance has been impressive, with Manchester United securing six consecutive Premier League wins, including a notable victory over Manchester City, which has put them in contention for a top-four finish. However, uncertainty looms over their futures with both players' positions at the club being questioned despite their recent success.

A 75-year-old piano teacher named John Goodwin, who was awaiting trial for six counts of aggravated felonious sexual assault, shot himself outside a New Hampshire courthouse while the jury was deliberating the case. The former student, now 24, testified that he did not report the assaults earlier due to embarrassment, while Goodwin's defense claimed the teacher's behavior was "touchy-feely" but not criminal. Goodwin was airlifted to a hospital with life-threatening injuries but his health status remained undisclosed as of the latest reports.

Amazon removed the controversial game "Rescue the Anorexia Girl" after it faced numerous complaints for its offensive and insensitive portrayal of anorexia. In the game, players throw food at a cartoon anorexic girl to prevent her from losing weight, with failure resulting in her death. Critics argue that the game stigmatizes and trivializes a serious mental illness, potentially discouraging those affected from seeking help.

Scientists are attempting to create an artificial brain modeled after the honeybee's, aiming to develop drones that think, sense, and act like these insects. This project, known as the Green Brain Project, involves mapping the honeybee's brain and recreating it with electronic circuits to control drones. So far, they have successfully cloned the vision part of the bee's brain and are testing drones in a specialized flying room at the University of Sheffield.

A newly-wed couple from Air Malta celebrated their marriage by taking a romantic flight over the Mediterranean in a passenger jet that flew in the shape of two giant hearts shortly after takeoff. The unusual flight path, which included two circuits around Malta and a section skirting the Italian coast, was arranged to celebrate the marriage of a pilot and a cabin crew member, with the couple's family, friends, and colleagues joining them for a short sight-seeing tour. The airline confirmed the couple was married at the airport earlier that day and that the flight was a romantic gesture rather than a public relations stunt.

At a Norwegian zoo on Easter Monday, a five-year-old giraffe named Melvin died after being gored by an eland antelope in an unprovoked attack. The tragic incident occurred when Melvin got his head stuck in the enclosure's fence, causing the eland to react aggressively. Shocked witnesses, including around 30 people and several children, reported that the event was extremely traumatic, with some visitors even crying.

A Belgian mother, Gitte Denteneer, was shocked and outraged to find a charge of 50 cents for heating up her baby's feeding bottle on her restaurant bill at the Rubens cafe in Leuven. Her tweet of the bill went viral, sparking widespread criticism of the restaurant manager's "stingy" practices. The Horeca Vlaanderen restaurant chain later clarified that such charges are uncommon and typically only applied if explicitly stated to customers beforehand.

North Korea has accused Mexico of illegally detaining one of its cargo ships, the Mu Du Bong, which ran aground off Mexico's coast in July. Mexico defended its action, citing that the ship's owner, North Korea's Ocean Maritime Management company, had violated United Nations sanctions. Meanwhile, North Korea denied wrongdoing and claimed that the crew members' human rights were being violated, while Mexican authorities stated that the crew was free and would soon be repatriated.

Prime Minister David Cameron plans to announce the provision of an additional 600,000 free childcare places per year, increasing from 15 to 30 hours per week for three- and four-year-olds and disadvantaged two-year-olds, aiming to support working families and reduce childcare costs. To fund this, the Conservatives propose reducing tax relief on pension contributions for individuals earning over £150,000. Cameron also emphasizes the importance of work in reducing poverty and improving life chances, arguing that the Conservative policies have led to more people working and a reduction in relative poverty since they came to power.

Manchester City secured their place in the Youth Cup final by scoring two late goals against Leicester City, extending their first-leg lead to 5-1 on aggregate. The goals came from substitutes Isaac Buckley and Brandon Barker, while Layton Ndukwu had briefly given Leicester hope with a penalty. This victory sets up a final against Chelsea for City, marking their return to the final after seven years.

During a nationally broadcast Q&A session, Russian President Vladimir Putin dismissed Western sanctions imposed after the annexation of Crimea and the conflict in eastern Ukraine, predicting they would not end soon. He defended Russia's decision to lift a ban on selling advanced air defense systems to Iran, asserting that such a system served as a defensive measure and was not a threat to Israel. The event, while appearing to offer an opportunity for dialogue, is seen by some as a showcase for Putin to address both domestic and international audiences rather than a genuine forum for questioning authority.

Tim Sherwood plans to bring Gary Gardner back into Aston Villa's first-team squad during pre-season to evaluate his potential for a permanent return to the Premier League. Gardner, who recently enjoyed a successful loan spell at Nottingham Forest and scored a notable free-kick in front of Sherwood, has expressed his desire to impress and potentially make an impact as a homegrown player. The 22-year-old, born in Solihull and a former England Under-21 player, joined Villa's academy at the age of seven and has shown loyalty to the club despite offers from other teams.

A stampede at the Tsunami nightclub in Santiago, Chile, during a performance by the British punk band Doom resulted in three deaths and injured over a dozen people, including seven in critical condition. The crush occurred when a large group tried to enter the club, causing a structure inside to collapse.
